scope.current_boundary: Teach scalar and vector definitions, properties, examples, classification and complete reporting only; do not teach vector addition, subtraction or resolution.
scope.previous_boundary_used: Uncertainty in derived quantities. Its magnitude-and-unit reporting prerequisite is recalled without reteaching uncertainty methods.
scope.next_boundary_checked: Resolving vectors into perpendicular components and Adding and subtracting coplanar vectors. This lesson establishes direction as a required vector property but does not teach any vector operation.

question_patterns_used.name: Definition
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Two exact controlled definition blocks are followed by plain-language explanations and contrasting examples.

question_patterns_used.name: Classification
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: A repeatable direction test and a fully worked mixed-list classification teach the required decision route.

question_patterns_used.name: Comparison
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Same-magnitude opposite forces, speed versus velocity, and complete versus incomplete reports make the distinction explicit.

questions_visited.why_selected: Tests a mixed table with familiar scalar and vector quantities.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Classify kinetic energy, power, work, acceleration, force and momentum.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Apply the direction requirement to each named quantity independently.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: A motion or force context can contain scalar quantities as well as vectors.

questions_visited.why_selected: Contrasts acceleration with speed and power.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Recognise acceleration as vector and speed and power as scalars.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Ask whether direction is part of each quantity, not whether it appears in a moving-object story.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Speed and velocity can share units but do not share scalar-vector status.
lesson_sections_informed: A scalar is complete without a direction
A common mistake: the unit or the story does not decide

questions_visited.why_selected: Includes a less intuitive scalar, electrical resistance, alongside acceleration and momentum.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Classify acceleration and momentum as vectors and electrical resistance as scalar.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use physical meaning and direction rather than a familiar unit or formula.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Unfamiliar quantities must be classified by the direction test, not a remembered short list.
lesson_sections_informed: A common mistake: the unit or the story does not decide

questions_visited.why_selected: Provides force and momentum as vectors among scalar alternatives.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Identify the all-vector choice in a mixed set.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Test every member of a proposed group before accepting it.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Selecting a group because it contains one vector fails if another member is scalar.

questions_visited.why_selected: Directly asks for both controlled definitions.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State the scalar and vector distinction precisely.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Recall that direction is absent from the scalar definition and required by the vector definition.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Calling a scalar merely a quantity with a unit omits the required magnitude-only distinction.
lesson_sections_informed: A scalar is complete without a direction
A vector needs a direction as well

questions_visited.why_selected: Checks power and temperature against momentum.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Classify two scalars and one vector after stating the definitions.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Test whether a direction would complete or change each report.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Momentum needs direction even though its magnitude has a compound unit.
lesson_sections_informed: A scalar is complete without a direction

questions_visited.why_selected: Reinforces the acceleration, resistance and momentum trio in a current paper format.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use direction as the decisive criterion for all three entries.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Electrical resistance does not become a vector because current is directional elsewhere in a circuit.

questions_visited.why_selected: Tests direction as the property that changes a vector while magnitude stays fixed.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Compare scalar and vector descriptions under a direction reversal.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify whether direction is part of the quantity before deciding whether reversal changes it.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: The same magnitude does not make two opposite vectors identical.
lesson_sections_informed: Worked example: same magnitude, different vector
